condition_priorities.multiple_conditions_logic: When patient has multiple conditions, priority is determined by organ damage risk & reversibility

priority_hierarchy.1_highest: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) - Kidney damage is irreversible, most restrictive diet
priority_hierarchy.2_very_high: Diabetes Type 2 - Risk of multiple organ complications if uncontrolled
priority_hierarchy.3_high: Cardiovascular Disease - Risk of sudden events (MI, stroke)
priority_hierarchy.4_moderate: Hypertension - Chronic damage but often reversible with diet
priority_hierarchy.5_moderate: Obesity - Risk factor for multiple diseases
priority_hierarchy.6_lower: Celiac Disease - Dietary management prevents complications but less immediately life-threatening

priority_order: 2. Sugar control (complex carbs only, HbA1c target < 7%)
2. Lipid management (saturated fat < 7%, increase soluble fiber)
1. Glycemic control (low GI foods, carb counting)

conflict_resolution.crd_vs_hypertension: Kidney disease takes priority - Phosphorus & potassium restriction overrides other considerations
conflict_resolution.diabetes_vs_cholesterol: Glycemic control is primary - Both benefit from complex carbs, whole grains
conflict_resolution.obesity_vs_protein: If CKD present: lower protein (0.8g/kg) overrides obesity management protein
conflict_resolution.general_rule: More severe/irreversible condition takes dietary priority

hypertension.reversal_potential: 50-60% can achieve normal BP without medication

type2_diabetes.reversal_potential: 50% achieve remission with weight loss + low GI diet

hypertension: 1-2 years: Organ damage begins (heart, kidneys, brain)
5+ years: Stroke, MI, or kidney failure risk increases 300-500%
diabetes: 10+ years: Death risk increases 2-3x normal population
ckd: Stage 3a: Mild kidney damage, 70% eGFR, asymptomatic
Stage 3b: Moderate damage, 45-59% eGFR, slight fatigue
Stage 4: Severe damage, 15-29% eGFR, anemia, high BP
Stage 5: Kidney failure, eGFR < 15, requires dialysis/transplant
